authority: Retrospective numerical rehearsal and prospective physical-test specification; not a blind experiment or physical admission.
candidate: Frozen Cartan-kernel rotor Hamiltonian with u=0.5 and D=sum_i(i-3.5)n_i; no per-line refitting.
calibration: One common frequency scale from the first odd transition energy.
One common dipole-squared/source-gain scale from that transition's spectral weight.
frozenInputs: Cartan charging branch, potential strength, charge geometry and source operator.
A frequency-independent source map; no frequency-dependent basis or gain correction.
Zero added local contact terms for the declared effective linear-source action. Physical matching remains unperformed.

withheldNumericalTargets.additionalLines: Next six odd transitions in energy order; compare their energies and dipole-squared weights.
withheldNumericalTargets.moments: Static response and derivative with respect to omega squared, neither used to calibrate the charge model.

controls: Single-pole O response with the same first-line calibration.
Single pole plus a constant fitted to the static response; one extra calibration datum.
Single pole plus constant and omega-squared term fitted to static response and slope; two extra calibration data.
toleranceAuthority: Chosen one-percent finite-model consistency threshold, not an experimental uncertainty or rigorous infinite-shell error bound.
physicalTestNeeds: Independently derived selector action on the physical charge/dipole operators and their spectral states.
A measured material/device spectrum, fixed geometry and field/volume calibration.
Matched contact terms and instrument response; declared damping and continuum contributions.
Unseen higher resonance frequencies and integrated line strengths, with uncertainty assessed before scoring.
failureRules: Reject the specified response law if held-out data require per-line gains, arbitrary pole shifts or a frequency-dependent source map.
A match to a refined solve of the same Hamiltonian establishes numerical predictive consistency only.
Do not call a source-map fit, an imposed constitutive kernel or an unobserved numerical replay a selector-specific physical prediction.
Do not use a narrow-band Taylor fit alone to establish the resonance spectrum.
